questions.stem: A company runs batch processing jobs that need high-performance processors. Which Amazon EC2 instance type is the best fit?

options.rationale: Storage optimized instances are for high local storage throughput.
Compute optimized instances suit compute-bound workloads such as batch processing and scientific modeling.
Memory optimized instances are for large in-memory data sets.
Accelerated computing instances use hardware accelerators such as GPUs.

questions.explanation: EC2 instance families: general purpose, compute optimized, memory optimized, accelerated computing, storage optimized and HPC optimized.

questions.stem: Which Amazon EC2 instance type is designed for workloads that process large data sets in memory, such as in-memory databases?

options.rationale: Compute optimized instances focus on processor performance.
Storage optimized instances focus on local disk throughput.
Memory optimized instances deliver fast performance for workloads that process large data sets in memory.
General purpose instances balance compute, memory and networking.

questions.explanation: Match the instance family to the bottleneck: CPU, memory, storage or accelerators.

questions.stem: Which Amazon EC2 instance type is designed for workloads that need high, sequential read and write access to very large data sets on local storage?

options.rationale: Memory optimized instances focus on RAM.
Compute optimized instances focus on CPU.
General purpose instances are balanced, not storage-focused.
Storage optimized instances deliver many low-latency random I/O operations per second for local storage.

questions.explanation: Storage optimized instances suit data warehousing, log processing and distributed file systems.

questions.stem: Which service runs code in response to events without provisioning or managing servers, and charges for the compute time used?

options.rationale: Lambda runs code on demand, scales automatically and bills for the compute time consumed.
EC2 requires you to provision and manage instances.
EKS runs Kubernetes clusters for containers.
Lightsail provides virtual private servers.

questions.explanation: Lambda is serverless compute: no servers to manage, automatic scaling and pay per use.

questions.stem: Which service lets a company run containers without managing the servers or clusters of Amazon EC2 instances underneath?

options.rationale: Auto Scaling adjusts the number of EC2 instances you still manage.
Fargate is a serverless compute engine for containers that works with Amazon ECS and Amazon EKS.
EBS provides block storage.
Lightsail provides virtual private servers that you manage.

questions.explanation: With Fargate you define the container and its resources, and AWS runs the infrastructure.

questions.stem: A company already uses Kubernetes and wants a managed Kubernetes service on AWS. Which service should it choose?

options.rationale: ECS is AWS's own container orchestrator, not Kubernetes.
Lambda runs functions, not Kubernetes clusters.
EKS is the managed Kubernetes service on AWS.
Auto Scaling adjusts instance counts; it is not a Kubernetes service.

questions.explanation: Containers on AWS: Amazon ECS (AWS orchestration), Amazon EKS (Kubernetes), and AWS Fargate as a serverless engine for both.

questions.stem: Which feature automatically adds or removes Amazon EC2 instances as demand changes?

options.rationale: Load balancers spread traffic but do not add or remove instances.
CloudFront caches content at edge locations.
AWS Config records configuration changes.
Auto Scaling adjusts the number of instances to match demand, which provides elasticity.

questions.explanation: Auto Scaling and load balancing work together: Auto Scaling sets capacity and the load balancer distributes traffic across it.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of Elastic Load Balancing?

options.text: Distributing incoming traffic across multiple targets such as EC2 instances
options.rationale: Load balancers spread requests across healthy targets in one or more Availability Zones.
That is the job of Auto Scaling.

options.text: Caching static content at edge locations
options.rationale: That describes Amazon CloudFront.

options.text: Encrypting data on Amazon EBS volumes
options.rationale: Encryption is a storage feature.

questions.explanation: Elastic Load Balancing improves availability by sending traffic only to healthy targets.

questions.stem: A company needs full control of the operating system on its application servers. Which compute service should it use?

options.rationale: With Lambda, AWS manages the operating system.
EC2 gives you control of the instance's operating system and software.
With Fargate, AWS manages the servers that run containers.
Athena is a query service, not a compute platform.

questions.explanation: The more control you need over the operating system, the more you lean toward EC2; the less you want to manage, the more you lean toward serverless.

questions.stem: Which TWO are serverless compute options on AWS? (Choose TWO.)

options.rationale: EBS is block storage, not compute.
Fargate runs containers without servers to manage.
Dedicated Hosts are physical servers dedicated to you.
Lambda runs functions without servers to manage.
EC2 instances are servers you manage.

questions.explanation: Serverless means AWS provisions, scales and manages the underlying infrastructure.
